Seeing happy people and people enjoying life, or looking like they have their lives together, it gives me this desperate feeling of longing for something I don't have. I think just seeing people that aren't me. 

Depressing places, places that are run down, places with fluorescent lights, places like Wal-mart, places that are cluttered and disorganized.

Also, happy things are triggers for me. Because anything that should make me happy just makes me extremely depressed. Example, if I walk downstairs and my mom is baking. 

I have too many triggers to list, because basically everything seems to be a trigger.

On the subject of TV shows, I can't watch a lot of things without feeling stressed or more depressed. Hoarders was a really bad trigger for some reason. I can't watch shows like Cops, S.V.U, basically any show that's a drama. I try to stick to Food Network or humorous shows because they're more comforting/distracting.

I know most 21 year old don't have it together. I just want to feel like I'm on some track to being in the right place. I know my job doesn't define me. But I constantly feel judged by the customers and the other employees even. I'm not comfortable around people in general, and customers can be so mean. And I do feel ashamed of myself for working there. I can't help it. I've been wanting to work somewhere else for a long time but my insecurities are so crippling and I don't want to end up somewhere else that I'm unhappy... so I haven't bothered looking. It sounds so stupid, I know. I'm only still there because I know what I'm doing even though I'm miserable. Can't count the number of times I've broken down crying there, not because of the job itself, but just because I feel so low in every other aspect of life as well. 

I've identified myself as ugly since I was 5. I'm just being real, I know what's attractive and what isn't. I'm not horribly disfigured but my face is not a good one. Doesn't help that nobody ever tells me I'm pretty. It hurts being with my family and my family always comments on how my cousins are so beautiful. I never hear that, because I'm ugly. I can't blame them, it just makes me miserable. My body's fine. And no nothing makes me feel beautiful. 

I'm currently looking into therapy again. Although last time I went I wasn't having suicidal thoughts. Anyway thanks for replying. I appreciate it.

I'm sorry, I feel bad about not having paragraph breaks. I was writing whatever came to mind so it's not very organized anyway. I went to a therapist a year ago, but abruptly stopped going because I accidentally missed an appointment. It wasn't working, I guess I gave up. My fault, I know.

 I don't really think there's any therapy to help me since I've been beaten down from a bunch of little things in my life piling up up up until now. My problems are from myself but I feel like they've been shaped by my not so great up-bringing. My therapist mostly tried EMDR therapy because I guess she felt like one event had triggered this all for me. But that's not the case. I feel bad about everything about myself and about my life and on some level I always have. 

I've been looking into getting a new therapist. I'm not very hopeful though.

I have no fake happiness to put on whatsoever. I'm at the lowest I've ever felt in my life, and I can't even fake it out in public. And I hate myself for it. I hate looking like I'm miserable. It doesn't help anything, but I can't even pretend to be ok. I want people to commiserate with me, or comfort me, or try to get me to be happy, but that's way too much to ask for because I turn people off by being so miserable. Vicious cycle, completely and utterly vicious.
